subject.title: File Browser: Remove ALLOWED_FILE_NAMES whitelist, add scope levels

question: Should OpenClaw support workspace-wide editing and/or host-filesystem browsing from Mission Control, and what permission boundary should replace the current bootstrap-file allowlist?
rationale: The request expands which files operator clients can read or mutate, and current main only approved a read-only workspace subset while leaving mutations and system scope to separate review.

options.title: Approve workspace-only CRUD first
options.body: Keep system filesystem browsing out of scope and settle a bounded `agents.workspace.*` mutation contract with root confinement, scopes, size/type limits, destructive-operation UX, audit posture, and real UI proof.

options.title: Keep read-only workspace browsing only
options.body: Treat current `agents.workspace.list/get` and the session file viewer as the supported browser path while leaving arbitrary workspace edits to terminal/editor workflows.

options.title: Open a separate system-scope design
options.body: If host filesystem browsing is desired, require a new security design for explicit opt-in, read/write limits, auditing, and recovery rather than folding it into the workspace issue.

recommendation.title: Approve workspace-only CRUD first
recommendation.body: Keep system filesystem browsing out of scope and settle a bounded `agents.workspace.*` mutation contract with root confinement, scopes, size/type limits, destructive-operation UX, audit posture, and real UI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged read-only workspace/file-viewer path and opened/closed the related maintainer-routed mobile workspace browser work.
